hook.line: When the day has gone badly, Spanish speakers sort it out in one breath: the good part, the bad part, the part that matters. Three little words do it for you.
hook.es: Lo bueno es que tenemos clientes.
hook.en: The good thing is we have customers.

examples.es: Lo bueno es que tenemos clientes.
examples.en: The good thing is we have customers.
The worst part was the wait.
What matters is to keep going.

examples.es: Lo malo es que no hay parqueadero.
examples.en: The bad thing is that there's no car park.

examples.es: Lo mejor es el olor del café.
examples.en: The best thing is the smell of the café.

rule:
Put *lo* in front of an adjective and you get "the ___ thing" or "the ___ part": *lo bueno*, *lo malo*, *lo difícil*, *lo importante*. It also works with *mejor* and *peor*: *lo mejor*, *lo peor*.

Then *es* (or *fue*, for something over):
*Lo bueno es que tenemos clientes.*
*Lo peor fue la espera.*

The *lo* never changes for gender or number, even if the thing is a *la espera*. Add *de* plus the topic at the end: *lo mejor es el olor del café*.

English needs extra words, "the ___ thing" or "the ___ part". Spanish just needs *lo*.
smallPrint: Teachers call this the neuter article *lo* used with an adjective to make an abstract noun.

readAndPick.es: Lo bueno es que tenemos clientes.
options: The bad thing is we have customers.
The good thing is we have customers.
The good thing is we had customers.
The best part was the wait.
The worst part was the wait.
The worst part is the wait.
What matters is to keep going.
What matters was to keep going.
What's hard is to keep going.

readAndPick.es: Lo malo es que no hay parqueadero.
options: The bad thing is that there's no car park.
The good thing is that there's a car park.
The easy part is starting.
The hard part is starting.
The hard part was starting.

readAndPick.es: Lo mejor es el olor del café.
options: The best thing is the smell of the café.
The worst thing is the smell of the café.

readAndPick.es: Lo mejor fue conocer a Vale.
options: The best part is meeting Vale.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *bueno* or *malo* and type the whole sentence: *Lo ___ es que tenemos clientes.* (The good thing is we have customers.)
yourTurn.answer: Lo bueno es que tenemos clientes.
yourTurn.why: Having customers is good news, so *bueno*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *es* or *fue* and type the whole sentence. The wait is over: *Lo peor ___ la espera.*
Type in Spanish: What matters is to keep going.
yourTurn.why: *Lo* plus the adjective, then *es* and the infinitive.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: The bad thing is that there's no car park.
yourTurn.answer: Lo malo es que no hay parqueadero.
yourTurn.why: A full clause after the adjective needs *es que*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: The hard part is starting.
yourTurn.why: *Difícil* does not change; only *lo* goes in front.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: The best thing is the smell of the café.
yourTurn.answer: Lo mejor es el olor del café.
yourTurn.why: *De* plus the place names whose smell or traffic it is.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: The worst thing is the traffic of the city.
yourTurn.answer: Lo peor es el tráfico de la ciudad.
yourTurn.why: *Lo peor*, then *es*, the thing, and *de* plus the place.

pitfalls.wrong: La buena es que tenemos clientes.
pitfalls.right: Lo bueno es que tenemos clientes.
pitfalls.why: Almost. For an idea rather than a noun, Spanish uses *lo*, not *la* or *el*.
Almost. After *lo* the adjective always stays in its basic masculine form.

pitfalls.wrong: Lo malo es no hay parqueadero.
pitfalls.right: Lo malo es que no hay parqueadero.
pitfalls.why: Almost. A full clause after *es* needs *que*.

personal: Think about your last week. Say one thing that was good, using *Lo bueno es que* or *Lo mejor fue*.
